transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think
Let’s start by checking if your Hotpoint dishwasher has power at all. When you press the power button, do any lights or the display come on?
Yes it has power, display is normal and it washes fine. The problem is just the door dropping open with no resistance.
Thanks for checking that out. Next, we need to see if the dishwasher knows the door is shut. When the door is closed and you press start, does it show the door is open (or a door light stays on)?
Yes the door closes and latches fine, and it starts and washes ok. No door open warning or anything like that. It's only when I open it that it drops down with no resistance.

Thanks for confirming that the door is recognised. Many dishwashers have a child or control lock, often marked by a key or padlock symbol, which stops the buttons working. The manual shows which buttons to hold to turn it off. Was the child / control lock on (and is it off now), or was it already off?
I don't think the child lock is on, the buttons all work fine. It's not a control problem, it's just the door dropping open when I open it. I heard a twang last week when it went.

Thanks for confirming that. Please switch the machine off at the socket and unplug it first. Look only — no tools on the catch or the lock. With the dishwasher switched off at the socket, look at the latch at the top of the door and the slot it clicks into on the tub, and check the door lines up squarely when you close it. Is the latch or catch broken, was something stopping it (now cleared), or does it all look fine?

Latch looks fine and the door closes square, it latches every time. It's not the catch, the door just has no resistance when opening. One side felt springy and the other loose. With a torch under the plinth I can see a loose spring hanging on the right side.

Thanks for checking the latch and strike again. Sometimes, a delay start feature—often shown as a countdown like 3h—or simply selecting a programme without confirming it can make the dishwasher appear as though it won't start. This is often mistaken for a fault when the machine is actually waiting for the timer to expire or for you to press Start. Was a delay start set or the programme not selected (and is it sorted), or was nothing like that set?
No delay start or anything like that, it starts and washes fine. It's only the door dropping open with no resistance, since the twang last week.

[Heading: Start control]
Thanks for checking those details. Since the dishwasher has power, recognises the door is shut, and has no child lock or delay settings active, the issue appears to lie with the start control side of the system. This requires an appliance engineer to diagnose properly. I am not recommending a specific part from this point, as it is best left to a professional to assess.
